why: Notice that the three panes do three different jobs: 5 spec rows under a named host, a month grid where only open Saturdays are buttons and closed dates such as Nov 28 stay plain text, and a slot list whose seat count disables full classes, caps the stepper and feeds the $65-per-seat button total, while the first open date is selected on load so no pane is ever blank.

Count 14 rows by 5 columns of maker's data (batch, scent with its wax colour dot, poured, cure end, left of 48 with a 3px meter), see that Cure ends is computed as poured plus 14 days, and notice that the same record drives a quick-view sheet whose shipping sentence has three states: curing ships on a date, ready ships today before 2 pm Central, and sold out disables the button and offers an email.

Notice that the summary is a small rules engine and not a sum: floor(tins / 6) times $12 appears as its own row only when earned, free shipping tests goods alone so the $130 class in this bag still leaves it $12 short with a 3px progress bar, the ship date is the latest cure date among the lines, and Remove answers with an Undo toast.

Trace one state object through 5 controls (4 department pills with counts, 3 size pills, 5 sort orders, a 9-checkbox sheet with live counts, removable chips) and see what each change touches: 20 cards refilter and glide with FLIP, 14 prices roll over 320ms, the centre count and the Show N button update, and an empty result offers Clear filters, all inside a 3px double-rule bar instead of a plain toolbar.

Notice that the 2fr 1fr 1fr 1fr columns let the address, hours in the shop's voice and a direct phone line outrank the link lists, the 4 Help items open a sheet of real policy sentences (carrier, $6 flat, lower 48, 1/4 in wicks) instead of dead links, and the full-width wordmark is one stacked CSS background, a 5px dot gradient in the page colour over wax-coloured gradients, clipped to the type.
